summary: Correctly rounded controller output no longer fails the post audit. The audit allowed each emitted coordinate half a unit in its last digit plus a fixed floating-point guard of 2.2e-16 mm. Half a unit in the last place of a coordinate exceeds that guard from 8 mm upwards, and lengths and sweeps formed from coordinates exceed it from about 2 mm, so a DXF imported with its exact geometry could fail generation and installation conformance although every coordinate was rounded correctly: an 8.0015 mm wide rectangle written as X8.002 at three decimals failed with POST_CUSTOM_AUDIT_FAILED while 8.0014 passed. Each comparison now allows floating-point roundoff of a few units in the last place of the values it reads, so the allowance grows with their magnitude. The counts are precision policy roles: outputPointRoundoffUlps (4) for endpoints and arc centres, and outputDerivedRoundoffUlps (32) for each term of the distance from a planned line, the radial distance from a planned arc, a path length and an arc sweep, with the count behind each stated in the policy. The audit reads them through cadOutputPointRoundoff and cadOutputDerivedRoundoff, which count magnitudes below 1 mm as 1 mm, and cadOutputFitting now takes the roundoff of each comparison. They replace outputRoundingGuardMm, so CAD_PRECISION_VERSION becomes 2. A straight move's emitted length is bounded by the exact longest and shortest paths its rounding allows instead of a first-order estimate, which missed the extra length when a nearly axis-aligned move's short side rounds across a unit. Every allowance is at least the one it replaces, so the audit accepts everything it accepted before. The motion mismatch diagnostic now states what the audit allows. This branch is merged with main at 0.0.791 (bbf73c47).
warning: Potentially breaking for installed posts: the post audit rules changed. Programs the audit rejected with POST_CUSTOM_AUDIT_FAILED (POST_AUDIT_MOTION_MISMATCH) can now be generated, and a post package that failed installation conformance only through this audit can now install. Nothing the audit accepted before is rejected. The allowance stays tight: an emitted coordinate one unit beyond correct rounding, swapped axes, a wrong sign, a wrong arc direction, a move left in place or a dropped half of a full circle still fail. Package contents and hashes, post engine API 1, saved-job engine 3 and controller output bytes are unchanged; every existing fixture produces byte-identical output. Audit results are not stored, so no installed package, saved revision or artifact is rewritten. The message text of POST_AUDIT_MOTION_MISMATCH changes; its code does not.

checklist.schema: No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, CAD, storage or journal schema change. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3. CAD_PRECISION_VERSION goes from 1 to 2 because the output roles changed; nothing stores it yet, so no cache or saved data is invalidated. No versioned audit path is added: rejecting correctly rounded output is not behaviour any caller needs to keep, and saved revisions and packages carry no audit result that an older rule would have to reproduce. If a later audit change can reject output that passes today, that change should introduce a recorded audit version for saved revisions.
checklist.events: No execution event, WebMCP tool, cancellation or input-version behavior change.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change.
checklist.auditAndOutput: Generation, numbering, encoding, line endings and controller-file rules are unchanged, and the audit only accepts or rejects, so successful output is byte-identical. Checks whose fixed guard is replaced: the event start and end points, arc centres, the points of a zero-length planned move, the distance from the planned line and the progress along it, the path length, the radial distance of arc endpoints and the arc sweep, together with the fallbacks for motion without rounding metadata. Unchanged: continuity between emitted blocks (exact copies), the backward-travel check (already scaled with its values), and the role, direction, full-circle and zero-length-path rules. A planned move that rounds to zero length is still rejected, and arcs whose radius is near the coordinate unit remain below the controller's resolution. POST_AUDIT_MOTION_MISMATCH now says that emitted coordinates may differ from the plan only by rounding to their last digit and the plan's endpoint tolerance.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change, and nothing is rewritten. Audit results and artifacts are not persisted: each generation reruns the audit from the saved revision, and reopening a stored post library checks structure and exact hash without rerunning conformance. Installation conformance uses the same audit, so a package refused before may now install; installed packages are unaffected.
checklist.verification: After the merge with main at 0.0.791: full Vitest 615 files and 6989 tests pass. Build, lint (zero findings, including the precision literal check), ui:check, post:docs:check, upid:conformance, Robofil 2.6.0 and minimal example post:conformance, Robofil machine-package:validate, release:check against origin/main and on its own, and the naming check pass. Single e2e specs pass: machine-package-install (2 tests, including generation and export of a controller artifact) and indexeddb-workbench (1 test; the private legacy cache acceptance test skips without its private snapshot, as on main). New tests: the 8.0015 width posts as X8.002 and the 8.0014 control as X8.001 through the installed Robofil post; sweeps of 200 log-uniform half-way values over [0.001, 1000) mm at 3 and 4 decimals, each posted as a bumped and notched rectangle and as a full circle; a nearly axis-aligned move whose short side rounds across a unit; negative tests for one unit beyond rounding in X and Y, swapped axes, a wrong sign, a move left in place, a dropped move, an arc centre one unit off, the wrong arc and full-circle direction and a dropped half circle, all still rejected, and installation conformance refusing a one-unit-beyond post; boundary tests through the real audit for each precision role, one input just inside and one just outside: an endpoint 7 and 8 ulps of 1000 mm beyond half a quantum, 5 and 6 ulps of 1 mm at 0.5 mm through the 1 mm floor, and a split point 31 and 33 ulps of 1000 mm off the line; ordering relations for the output roles and a recorded known limit for 12-decimal posts above about 563 mm; and an end-to-end case from the reviewer's DXF through package installation, import, save, stored saved revision and artifact generation. Measured through the Robofil post with plans at endpoint tolerance 0: main accepted 2711 of 4500 half-way programs at 3 decimals and 2750 of 4500 at 4 decimals, this release accepts all 9000; with the default 0.001 mm plan tolerance both accept all 9000. A randomized differential of 400000 linear and circular cases found no case main accepts and this release rejects. Mutations before the merge: restoring the fixed guard fails 9 tests and restoring main's audit fails 10; doubling the ulp counts fails 2 and doubling the half-unit terms fails 4. On the precision policy, besides the version pin: outputPointRoundoffUlps x10 fails 5 tests and x0.1 fails 6, outputDerivedRoundoffUlps x10 fails 3 and x0.1 fails 5, removing the 1 mm floor fails 3, a fixed epsilon fails 14, and ignoring the term count fails only the policy exactness test, because no audit input reaches the length or sweep roundoff. Controller output for the canonical plans through Robofil and the minimal example, the UPID examples, the Robofil package fixtures, no-lead-rectangle.dxf and a 78-line production DXF is byte-identical under main's audit at 0.0.791 and under this release, and identical to this branch before the merge; only the new half-way DXF differs, which main refuses. No physical-machine or controller verification is claimed.

testedPosts.scope: Robofil 2.6.0 conformance, its package fixtures and golden output pass unchanged; half-way coordinates at 3 decimals, and at 4 decimals with its precision limit widened in tests only, post and pass the audit. No physical-machine verification.

publicNotes.summary: Controller files whose coordinates lie half-way between two output digits no longer fail the output check.
changes: A drawing whose coordinates round correctly to the post's last digit, such as 8.0015 mm written as 8.002, now generates instead of failing with POST_CUSTOM_AUDIT_FAILED.
The output check still rejects a coordinate one unit beyond correct rounding, swapped axes, a wrong sign and a wrong arc direction.
The motion mismatch message says what the output check allows.
publicNotes.compatibility: Controller output that generated before is unchanged byte for byte. Programs and post packages refused only by this check can now be generated or installed. Installed posts and saved revisions are not rewritten.
publicNotes.action: Check newly generated programs as usual in controller graphics and a supervised dry run, especially programs that failed before this release.
